articles.title: Intes 6-inch Maksutov, Extended-use Report
articles.summary: This extended-use report by Jay Freeman describes five months of experience with an Intes 6-inch f/10 Maksutov telescope. The author expresses high satisfaction with the instrument, praising its sparkling optical quality, compact design, affordability, and ease of use. The telescope demonstrates excellent performance for both high-magnification planetary and double-star observations, as well as low-magnification wide-field deep-sky views, showcasing remarkable versatility.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines an activities calendar for January and February, detailing various astronomy-related events. It includes dates and times for star parties at multiple parks (Houge, Henry Coe, Fremont Peak), observational astronomy classes, and general meetings with board meetings. Key astronomical information such as sunset times and moon phases are also provided for each event.

articles.title: Return to the Red Planet
articles.summary: The article recounts an attendee's experience at a free public presentation titled "Return to the Red Planet," co-hosted by NASA Ames Research Center and The Planetary Society. Held on November 14th, the event featured Dr. Ben Bova, former editor of Analog and OMNI magazines, who spoke on "MARS, Who Cares and Why?" Dr. Bova emphasized the potential profound effects of scientific discoveries on daily life, illustrating this with the historical impact of the polio vaccine.

articles.title: Mars, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article compiles insights from multiple speakers on Mars exploration, primarily focusing on the search for life and the presence of water on the Red Planet. Dr. Bova discussed the psychological impact of discovering Martian bacteria, Dr. Carr presented geological evidence for subsurface water and the origin of meteorite ALH84001, and Dr. McKay detailed his search for fossilized life. Donna Shirley then outlined JPL's Mars Surveyor Program, revealing plans for future orbiter and lander missions aimed at investigating life, climate, and resources, with an increased focus on life detection and sample return following the ALH84001 announcement.

articles.title: Mak, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article reviews the Intes 6-inch f/10 Maksutov telescope, praising its uncompromising optical quality, portability, and relatively low price compared to high-end refractors, Newtonians, and Schmidt-Cassegrains of similar aperture. While it effectively competes with smaller premium refractors and offers a better balance of performance and portability than larger instruments, the author notes downsides such as a long cool-down time, a quirky focuser, and the tendency for its corrector plate to gather dew. Despite these minor issues, the author highly recommends the instrument for its value and performance.

articles.title: Mars, continued from page 2
articles.summary: This article snippet details an attendee's positive experience at an event, where they enjoyed presentations by four speakers and collected promotional materials. The author encourages fellow San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) members who attended to share their notes and promises to mention similar future events in the club newsletter. A JPL website is also provided for updates on Mars Surveyor missions.

articles.title: BOB LOOKS UP for January, or "Orions other side"
articles.summary: This January observing guide highlights the benefits of cold, dry air for both visual astronomy and astrophotography, including improved transparency and reduced reciprocity failure for film. It suggests observing targets such as NGC2022 and the double star 23 ORI in the northern part of Orion, as well as the lunar crater Gassendi and its rimae system, which will be well-lit on January 18th-19th.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly throughout the year, from January to December. This statement clarifies its publication frequency and affiliation, with an example issue cited from January 1997.

articles.title: Eye on Everything
articles.summary: This article discusses the resignation of several board members, particularly Mark Wagner, and the controversy surrounding his status due to changes in club bylaws. It details amendments requiring board members to be club members and limiting officer terms to one year, raising questions about their retroactivity. The author invites member feedback on these issues and announces upcoming board elections in February.

articles.title: Update on Henry Coe Park
articles.summary: The ranger at Henry Coe Park will not move into his new residence until at least April, as the move is contingent upon paving completion. Consequently, the park's usual site will remain accessible for use until that time.

articles.title: First light, Astro-Physics 180mm f/9 EDT
articles.summary: This article describes a "first light" experience with a new Astro-Physics 180mm f/9 EDT telescope at Fremont Peak, California. Despite poor seeing conditions, the author was impressed by the sharp and contrasty images of deep sky objects, Saturn, and the Moon, praising the telescope's robust build quality. The report also briefly mentions an inspection of the corral area at the campground.

articles.title: Notes To Help You Make Better Use Of Comet Comments
articles.summary: Don Machholz's "Comet Comments" is a monthly column, active since 1978, designed to inform amateur astronomers about new comet discoveries and aid in observing brighter comets. The column provides essential information including comet news, observing tips, ephemerides (predicted positions), and orbital elements for comets brighter than magnitude 11. It also includes a detailed guide on how to interpret all provided data, such as Universal Time, Right Ascension, Declination, predicted magnitude, and various orbital parameters.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - Jan 1997
articles.summary: The 'Celestial Calendar - Jan 1997' article provides a detailed astronomical guide for the month, listing lunar phases with precise timings in PST. It also includes comprehensive ephemeris data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Sun, detailing their distances, magnitudes, rise, transit, and set times, along with their celestial coordinates. Additionally, it specifies astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and highlights the 'Darkest Saturday Night' on January 4th for optimal viewing.

articles.title: Don Machholz
articles.summary: Don Machholz provides an update on several comets, debunking circulating stories of "mysterious objects" near Comet Hale-Bopp, which he states is behaving normally. He notes that Hale-Bopp will be visible in the morning sky by late January, while also mentioning Comet Tabur's unpredictable dimming, the return of Periodic Comet Wirtanen with its nucleus measured by Hubble, and the visibility of Periodic Comet Wild 2.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for four comets: C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), C/1996 Q1 (Tabur), 46P/Wirtanen, and 81P/Wild 2. For each comet, tables list daily coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation from the Sun, sky visibility (Morning or Evening), and apparent magnitude, spanning from late December to early February.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed table of orbital elements for four comets: Hale-Bopp, Tabur, P/Wirtanen, and P/Wild 2. It lists parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period, along with their respective MPC references. The data appears to be part of an ephemeris from January 1997.

articles.title: Celestron 5 Telescope:
articles.summary: This document is an advertisement for a used Celestron 5 Telescope, available for sale. The listing highlights its features such as special coatings, various oculars, tripod, wedge, case, camera adapter, and spotting scope, emphasizing its suitability for celestial photography and as a 1300mm camera lens. The seller, Rick, is asking $850 for the package, which was originally purchased for $1400 in 1987 and is valued over $2000 new with included options.

articles.title: Astro-Physics 155mm f9 EDT APO,
articles.summary: This document is an advertisement for a used Astro-Physics 155mm f9 EDT APO optical tube assembly. Described as being in great condition and producing beautiful images, this Super ED triplet APO comes with its case and 2" and 1 1/4" Astro-Physics adapters. The asking price is $3195, and contact information is provided for Rich.

articles.title: Celestron Pro 9x63 binocular with case. $160
articles.summary: This is a classified advertisement for a used Celestron Pro 9x63 binocular, which includes a case, available for $160. Contact information for seller Rich Neuschaefer is provided for inquiries.

articles.title: Brand new Celestron C90 spotting scope model 81011
articles.summary: This document is an advertisement listing a brand new Celestron C90 spotting scope (model 81011) with accessories and a Celestron hard case for $275. Additionally, it offers a 20" by 2 1/8" astronomy Pyrex glass mirror blank from Newport Glass for $700. Contact information for Loran is provided.

articles.title: Celestron Firstscope 60 EQ:
articles.summary: A Celestron Firstscope 60 EQ refractor telescope, less than 3 months old and in "like-new" condition, is listed for sale for $90. It comes with 20mm, 12.5mm eyepieces, and a 2X .96" Barlow lens. Interested parties can contact Mike at 408-256-0881.

articles.title: ASTRONOMY magazines, free to good home. 1989 - newer.
articles.summary: Bill Lockman is offering a collection of ASTRONOMY magazines, dating from 1989 to newer issues, for free to anyone interested. The document also includes general guidelines for submitting free non-commercial advertisements related to astronomy, providing contact details for the editor.

articles.title: Paul Barton
articles.summary: This document outlines an equipment loan program, likely for an astronomy club, managed by Paul Barton. It lists various telescopes and other astronomical equipment, their current borrowers, due dates, and availability status, along with notes on specific items and a waiting list for popular scopes. SJAA members are eligible to borrow equipment by contacting Paul Barton.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors for an organization, detailing each individual's position (President, Treasurer, Secretary, Director), name, and a corresponding contact phone number. It serves as a direct reference for the organization's leadership team.

articles.title: Editor
articles.summary: This document identifies Lew Kurtz as the editor, providing a contact phone number. It references the 'SJAA Ephemeris' from January 1997, suggesting it is a contact or editorial page from that publication.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships at various price points, including an optional Sky & Telescope subscription. It provides instructions for payment via check and submission either in person at an SJAA meeting or by mail to the treasurer, including contact information and a mailing address.
